items.title: 'Swachh Space': India's Plan To Clean Up Its Orbital Trash By 2030
points: India has unveiled an ambitious "Swachh Space" vision that aims to make the country's space activities debris free by 2030.
It is estimated that over 100 million pieces of man-made junk float in space.

Announcing the goal of making space debris-free, Union Minister of State for Science Jitendra Singh said on November 5 that India is emerging among the early global pioneers in space debris removal and is advancing capabilities that will help make outer…

items.title: Cuddalore Poultry Crisis: 50,000 Chickens Dead, Tamil Nadu Farmers In Disaster
points: Mohan, a poultry farmer in Tamil Nadu's Cuddalore district, is a shattered man.
He has lost 7,000 birds over the past week, watching his investment and livelihood crumble as an unidentified disease sweeps through poultry farms in the district.
Mohan is among several poultry farmers caught in a crisis that has reportedly claimed nearly 50,000 chickens across several villages in Cuddalore over the past six days.
A single chick costs around Rs 47-48, while a 50-kg bag of poultry feed costs between Rs 2,500 and Rs 2,600.
Electricity bills alone run into Rs 10,000 to Rs 20,000.
We just sit here helplessly, having invested Rs 40 to Rs 50 lakh.
District authorities, however, estimate the number of dead birds at around 26,000, significantly lower than the nearly 50,000 deaths reported by farmers.

items.title: Ammonia-Powered Bulk Carrier Takes on Green Fuel in Australian First
points: The ammonia-powered bulk carrier Mineral Europa receives green ammonia during a ship-to-ship bunkering operation at the Port of Port Hedland, Australia.

Photo: Fortescue Australia has completed its first green ammonia bunkering operation involving an ammonia-powered bulk carrier, marking another step toward bringing alternative fuels into commercial shipping.

The operation took place earlier this week at the Port of Port Hedland in Western Australia, where the 300-meter Mineral Europa received certified green ammonia from a bunker vessel before entering port to load iron ore bound for China.
According to a joint announcement from Fortescue, Pilbara Ports and CMB.TECH, the ship-to-ship transfer took approximately two hours and was completed successfully at 8:42 a.m. local time.
In 2024, its Fortescue Green Pioneer completed ammonia-fueled propulsion trials in Singapore, demonstrating the technology aboard a converted offshore support vessel.
The Port Hedland operation builds on an earlier ship-to-ship ammonia transfer trial at nearby Dampier in September 2024, which helped establish procedures for handling ammonia between vessels.

Finnish Police/Handout via REUTERS HELSINKI, Nov 5 (Reuters) – A Finnish court on Thursday jailed the Russian captain and an Azerbaijani crew member of the cargo ship Fitburg for aggravated sabotage over damage to two subsea telecommunications cables in…
Finland on December 31 seized the vessel in the Gulf of Finland while it was en route from Russia to Israel, on suspicion that it had damaged cables running from Helsinki to Estonia.
The Helsinki District Court sentenced the captain to 3 years and 6 months in prison and the crew member to 2 years and 10 months.
It said in a statement the two acted intentionally when the ship dragged an anchor chain and anchor shank along the seabed for around 130 km (81 miles).

items.title: Yen Rises on Haven Demand as CIBC, Nomura See Room for More Gain
points: The Japanese yen rose as a selloff in US technology shares led traders to seek safer assets — a trend that strategists at CIBC and Nomura expect will continue.

The yen strengthened as much as 0.6% against the US dollar to 157.54 on Thursday, outperforming all of its Group of 10 peers after a Democratic sweep in this week’s US midterms led to concern about artificial intelligence investments that hit US stocks.
“If the AI trade continues to unwind, investors will be looking for somewhere to go,” said Sarah Ying, head of foreign-exchange strategy at CIBC.
She expects the yen to strengthen to 148 against the dollar by the end of 2027, a more-than-6% rise from current levels, as investors flee dollar-denominated assets.

Dominic Bunning, head of Group of 10 strategy at Nomura, said the firm remains long on the Japanese yen against the dollar, calling it the “consistent best FX trade” in an environment in which equities and yields are both declining.

items.title: 7 Killed After Speeding Truck Runs Over People In Jharkhand: Cops
points: Seven people were killed when a speeding 18-wheeler truck ran over them late Thursday night in Jharkhand's Khunti district, police said.
The accident occurred near the Jone-Ludru turn, before Poda, on the Karra-Torpa main road within the Karra police station area.
The victims have been identified as Pako Devi, Kasila Devi, Manhu Devi, Golu Kumar, Anjali Kumari, Tuti Kumari, and 12-year-old Saurabh Nayak.
Khushbu Kumari, who was injured in the accident, is undergoing treatment at Khunti Sadar Hospital.
According to eyewitnesses, at around 9:45 p.m. on Thursday, a scooter rider lost control and fell into bushes near a culvert close to the Jone-Ludru turn.
Meanwhile, a speeding truck coming from the Torpa side ran over the people standing along the roadside in which six people died on the spot.
At around 11:15 p.m. on Thursday, 12-year-old Saurabh Nayak also succumbed to his injuries during treatment, raising the death toll to seven.
Local residents alleged that the driver of the truck (JH 02 AJ 1377) was under the influence of alcohol.

items.title: Inmarsat Maritime Safety Data Hub to help shipping weather the storm
points: Inmarsat Maritime recently launched the Maritime Safety Data Hub, which combines Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) call data with an industry-first analysis of maritime safety broadcasts.
Complementing this unique dataset is a series of interviews with maritime safety experts conducted by Inmarsat’s research partner, SeaFocus International, as part of the Safety Hub’s development.
Managing weather hazards Among the 106,975 maritime safety broadcasts made in 2025, 2.6% were marked ‘urgent’.
Of these, Inmarsat analysis identified 84.6% as related to weather, with storms and gales representing 75% and 20% of meteorological hazards, respectively.
Despite accounting for just 4% of these hazards, cyclones were responsible for over 99% of urgent weather messages, reflecting their disproportionate impact on safety.

Persistent challenges, evolving risks While Inmarsat received fewer GMDSS calls in 2025 (741) than in 2023 (788) and 2024 (801), the three-year trend remains broadly consistent with historical averages, reflecting how established safety challenges persist…

items.title: Iran says five tankers and tugboat caught fire in Hormuz
points: Five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and army said in separate statements, according to local media on Thursday.
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

“Last night… a large oil tanker attempting to pass through the illegal passageway south of the Strait of Hormuz suffered a fire after striking a mine and was brought to a halt,” the Guards told Fars news agency.

“Early this morning, a violating oil tanker — navigating through an unsafe area east of the Strait of Hormuz — caught fire and came to a halt after striking a naval mine,” the army said, according to the official IRNA news agency.
“Today at around noon, two more oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the unsafe waters east of the Strait of Hormuz,” said another army statement carried by IRNA.

items.title: IMO Council backs second term for Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez
points: The IMO Council has decided to extend the mandate of Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez for a second four-year term, from 1 January 2028 to 31 December 2031.

Announcing the decision on 4 November during the Council’s 138th session in London, Council Chair Mr. Victor Jimenez (Spain) congratulated the Secretary-General on behalf of the IMO Council and confirmed that the decision would be submitted to the IMO…
“I am deeply grateful to the Members of the Council and all Members of the Organization for their continued trust and support.

I remain committed to following your guidance and contributing to our collective efforts in support of global shipping and seafarers.” Mr. Dominguez is the tenth Secretary-General of the International Maritime Organization.
He was first elected by the IMO Council, comprising 40 IMO Member States, at its 129th session in July 2023 for a four-year term beginning on 1 January 2024.
His election was approved by the IMO Assembly at its 33rd session in December 2023.

items.title: Fujairah’s LSMGO premium over Singapore widens by around $180/mt since September

Fujairah’s LSMGO monthly average reached around $1,720/mt in October, the highest since November 2021.
The port’s premium over Singapore was around $460/mt on 19 October.
Fujairah’s fuel oil stocks averaged 9% lower in October so far than across September, Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) and S&P Global data showed.
Fujairah’s VLSFO price traded at a discount to Singapore’s of up to around $20/mt on each weekday from 27 October to 2 November.
Singapore’s residual fuel oil inventories averaged 6% lower in October than in September.
The gap reversed on 3 November, when Fujairah’s VLSFO price rose around $20/mt and Singapore’s fell around $20/mt.
Fujairah’s VLSFO now trades at a premium of around $20/mt over Singapore, against around $50/mt on 1 September.

items.title: Global trade is growing. The capacity it needs doesn’t stop at the quay
points: A container terminal can handle more cargo than ever before and still leave its customers waiting.
For much of the past 15 years, investment in landside infrastructure has lagged behind the changing demands of trade.
Europe’s Northern Range ports handled around 46 million TEU last year at almost 100% utilisation, and will need room for at least 53 million TEU by 2030 and 62 million by 2035.
Igor van den EssenChief Executive, Africa & Europe, APM TERMINALS The obvious response is to build.
The pressure is only going to increase By 2030, around 900 container vessels above 15,000 TEU are expected to be in service, twice as many as today.
Much of the world’s older port infrastructure, particularly in Europe, was designed for a different generation of ships.
Our hub terminals supporting the Gemini network, including Rotterdam, Bremerhaven, Algeciras and Tangier, now handle more than 70% more moves per hour than a decade ago.

items.title: Marlow Navigation welcomes MPC Oceanic Group as strategic shareholder
points: MPC Oceanic Group AG, and the shareholders of Marlow Navigation Co. Ltd. (“Marlow”), today signed an agreement under which MPC Oceanic Group will acquire a 41% stake in Marlow.

The transaction builds on a relationship between the two groups spanning more than a decade and establishes a long-term strategic partnership, while preserving Marlow’s operational independence, established brand and existing leadership.

With more than 1,300 shore-based professionals across 13 countries and in excess of 16,000 crew serving on board vessels at any given time, the Marlow Group provides crew management services to shipowners and operators for more than 1,150 vessels trading…
MPC Oceanic Group is a Hamburg-based, publicly listed group of companies that builds, invests in and operates businesses and assets in the maritime and energy sector.
The group is active in eight countries and manages and operates more than 400 vessels and energy assets.
Strategic rationale: complementary capabilities and long-term continuity MPC Oceanic Group and Marlow have a long-standing relationship and share a partnership-driven approach to maritime services.

items.title: Environment Committee of the European Parliament calls on the Commission to not approve beaching yards under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation
points: On 4 November, a large majority of the Members of the European Parliament in the Committee on the Environment, Climate and Food Safety of the European Parliament (ENVI Committee) voted against the inclusion of two beaching shipbreaking yards in the 16th…
These two yards, Shree Ram and YSI Recyclers, located in Alang-Sosiya, India, have been preliminarily approved by the European Commission to recycle EU-flagged ships.

Through their objection, MEPs argue that yards using the so-called “beaching method”, i.e. scrapping ships on tidal mudflats, cannot be accepted on the EU List as they do not meet EU standards for environmental and workers protection [1].

The ENVI Committee is very clear in its wording: “including a facility that practises the beaching method for the dismantling of end-of-life ships in the European List would be against the intention and the letter of the [Ship Recycling Regulation]”.

items.title: AskChief surpasses 100-vessel milestone in under a year and opens its specialised maritime AI to the wider market
points: AskChief, Specialised AI for maritime Technical and HSQE teams, today announced that it is opening its platform to the wider market after surpassing 100 vessels in under a year of live use with shipowners and ship managers.
Across customer deployments, use of AskChief typically triples within the first 90 days, reflecting how quickly it becomes part of teams’ daily work.
AskChief has worked with maritime operators including Seanergy Maritime, Castor Ships, Iblea, Delia, IMECS (part of the ITOCHU Group) and others.
Their Technical and HSQE teams have helped shape AskChief Technical and AskChief Compliance around real tasks onboard vessels and in shore-based offices.
That’s the kind of tool a modern fleet should be running,” said Stamatis Tsantanis, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Seanergy Maritime Holdings Corp.
Specialised AI moves the work forward,” said Michalis Gkontas, Co-Founder and CEO of AskChief.

items.title: Wärtsilä dual-fuel engine and propulsion solution selected for Delfin Midstream’s pioneering project
points: Technology group Wärtsilä has secured an order to supply the engines and thrusters for the first Floating Liquefied Natural Gas (FLNG) vessels being built at Samsung Heavy Industries (SHI) for the U.S. -based Delfin LNG project.

The propulsion solutions will support efficient, reliable and environmentally sustainable operations for the offshore LNG facility, helping accelerate the development of new LNG export infrastructure.
The order was booked by Wärtsilä in Q2 2026.

The chosen propulsion arrangement, including the ability to hoist the thrusters for inboard maintenance prior to the hurricane season, is part of the solution designed for reliable operations and to ensure the safety of crew and asset,” comments Björn…
Wärtsilä worked closely with the project partners during the feed engineering phase to develop a propulsion arrangement tailored to the vessel’s unique requirements.
Wärtsilä will supply three Wärtsilä 46DF dual-fuel engines together with an advanced exhaust gas treatment system featuring SCR with Oxicat technologies.

items.title: Successful Sea Trials for Becker Daggerboard Technology
points: Becker Marine Systems’ Anti-Drift Daggerboard technology has been successfully tested during sea trials of the new Airbus transport vessel ‘Spirit of Toulouse’.

Equipped with specially developed Anti-Drift Daggerboards from Becker Marine Systems, the vessel combines innovative wind-assisted propulsion with advanced hydrodynamic technology to improve overall efficiency.
The project marks an important milestone for Becker Marine Systems and demonstrates the role of advanced hydrodynamic technology in supporting efficient wind-assisted propulsion.

Becker Marine Systems’ Anti-Drift Daggerboard system has been successfully tested during sea trials of the ‘Spirit of Toulouse’, a new RoRo cargo vessel designed to transport Airbus aircraft components across the Atlantic.

The 168-metre-long vessel was built for the French shipping company Louis Dreyfus Armateurs (LDA) and will operate between Airbus production sites in Europe and its final assembly facility in Mobile, Alabama (USA).

One of the vessel’s key features is its innovative propulsion concept: Six 35-metre-high Flettner rotors supplied by Finnish manufacturer Norsepower harness wind energy to generate additional thrust, thereby reducing fuel consumption.

items.title: StormGeo Partners with China Classification Society to Advance Digital Emissions Verification in China
points: StormGeo, a global provider of weather intelligence and maritime technology and part of Alfa Laval’s Ocean Division, has joined forces with the China Classification Society (CCS) to help digitalize emissions data sharing and verification.
The partnership is a key step in StormGeo’s efforts to grow in China and better support local shipping customers.
“China plays a leading role in the transformation of global shipping, and we want StormGeo to be an active and trusted partner in that development.

We are investing in our local capabilities, partnerships and technology to support that ambition, and our partnership with CCS is an important step in this long-term commitment,” said Espen Martinsen, Chief Commercial Officer at StormGeo.
StormGeo currently supports approximately 700 vessels on GHG emissions and vessel performance in the Chinese market and has clear ambitions to significantly expand its presence in the coming years.

items.title: Everllence and Babcock Sign Strategic MoU to Support Future Arrowhead 140 Programme
points: Everllence and Babcock International Group (Babcock), the defence company, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore a strategic partnership that will strengthen the delivery and future development of the globally successful Arrowhead…
The two companies signed the MoU at Euronaval, the major, international, naval defence and maritime security exhibition, in Paris.
Under the proposed partnership framework, Everllence would become a strategic partner for power and propulsion systems across future Arrowhead programmes.

The collaboration originates from discussions regarding Babcock’s Arrowhead 140 platform, and creates a framework to evaluate opportunities, including future requirements within the Danish naval market – such as its Arctic Frigate project – and other…

The Arrowhead 140 is a modern, modular frigate design developed by Babcock and intended as a flexible base-platform that different navies can customise with their own weapons, sensors, propulsion and combat systems.

items.title: US copper cathode imports to slow in November as October beats breakbulk record
points: US breakbulk imports of copper cathode are on track to exceed 230kt in October, a monthly record, but Kpler expects deliveries to fall to 100kt in November now that the LME–COMEX arbitrage has closed.
The pending Section 232 tariff verdict will decide whether the US draws in more copper, and what happens to the estimated 2 million tons of cathode already on US shores.
Record-breaking imports October deliveries of copper cathode in breakbulk are on track to exceed 230kt as the month draws to a close.
This comfortably surpasses the previous record of 198kt set in July and follows more than 140kt in each of August and September.
These outsized imports have been spurred by the arbitrage between LME and COMEX copper prices which averaged $500/t between May and early August, but has since narrowed to a close.

items.title: West Bengal govt’s new investment policy promotes job-linked growth, incentives for plant and machinery
points: The West Bengal Investment Promotion Policy, 2026 that comes into effect from May 9, 2026 the day when the first BJP government in the State took office, offers up to 120 % assistance to a thrust sector unit in a priority area on the share of fixed capital…
“The previous government had cheated the industrialists,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said while unveiling the much-awaited policy document for the revival of industries in the State.
The Chief Minister said that West Bengal will try to emerge from the “bad experiences” as far as industry was concerned of the previous two regimes.

The ceiling for the amount of assistance given on the share of (FCI) made in plant and machinery is 100 % for regular units, 110 % for units in thrust sectors or priority areas, and 120 % for thrust-sector units located in priority areas.

items.title: MARAD Approves $1 Billion Offshore Crude Oil Export Port Off Louisiana
points: The Trump administration has approved a $1 billion offshore crude oil export project off the coast of Louisiana, clearing a major regulatory hurdle for a facility designed to load some of the world’s largest oil tankers directly in the Gulf of Mexico.

U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced Thursday that the Maritime Administration (MARAD) has approved the deepwater port license application for Blue Marlin Offshore Port, a project capable of exporting up to 2 million barrels of crude oil per day.
The facility will be located approximately 99 miles off Cameron Parish, Louisiana, in West Cameron Block 509.
“Building this port will unleash domestic production, create more than 1,000 good-paying construction jobs along the Gulf of America, and open vital supply lines to global markets,” Duffy said.

The approval is the fourth deepwater port project cleared under the Trump administration, following the Texas GulfLink crude oil export project, Delfin LNG off Louisiana, and the $8.2 billion ST LNG project approved off Texas last week.

It submitted its interim report to the government on Thursday (November 5, 2026).
According to the report, around 12 lakh candidates have applied for the MPSC Group C Combined Preliminary Examination 2026, for which more than 5,000 vacancies have been advertised.
With government departments submitting requisitions for over 11,000 additional posts, the committee has recommended including these vacancies through a corrigendum.

Bank accounts to be opened for children studying in government schools in Bihar
points: Along with this, instructions have been issued to ensure that every child has an individual or joint bank account in a government or nationalised bank.
Education Department’s Director (Administration) has sent a letter to all District Education Officers (DEOs) and District Programme Officers (DPOs) in this regard.
The letter states that the Central government has emphasised opening bank accounts for everyone in government banks under its financial inclusion initiative since 2014.
A birth certificate is required for opening a bank account.
Keeping these requirements in mind, the Education Department has directed all government schools to maintain the birth certificates of every enrolled child in their official records.

The Department has instructed the headmasters of all the government schools to establish contact with the managers of nearby government or nationalised bank branches and ensure that bank accounts are opened for all children enrolled in their schools.

items.title: Keralam’s Gavi to go green, eyes energy neutrality
points: The Kerala Forest Development Corporation (KFDC), which manages the forest settlement, has initiated measures to curb pollution from vehicles and reduce environmental impact of tourism.
The green push follows Forest Minister Shibu Baby John’s public backing for a proposal to make Gavi carbon-neutral.
Electric buses will be stationed at the Vallakkadavu checkpost to ferry visitors who book trips to Gavi.
A solar-powered electric fence is also being erected at a cost of ₹30 lakh to ensure visitor safety.
The authorities, meanwhile, have also mooted a proposal to convert the Kerala State Road Transport Services (KSRTC) buses operating services to Gavi into electric vehicles in a phased manner.
Visitor numbers exceeded 2,000 on certain days, far above the limit envisaged in the area’s management plan, which remains in force until 2030, officials said.
Spread across nearly 1,100 acres, the KFDC-managed estate has cardamom plantations, with tourism emerging as an important additional source of revenue.
